chapter: Baton Rouge heroes: Guy Kelly and Buddy Petit
title: Buddy Petit visiting Papa's shoe shop
summary: Buddy Petit would bring his cornet to the shoe shop during Prohibition, play new tunes with Papa's harmonica, and praise Joe as a future clarinetist.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Let me ask you about Buddy Petit. When did you first come across him?
Buddy Petit never did any kind of work. But I remember Buddy Petit, because my Dad had a shoe shop and my Dad used to do a little bootlegging. I don't like to

say that now, but we can't do him nothin' now. But everybody did a little legging. Now, remember, this was during Prohibition. And Buddy would come around there, and bring his horn -- and like I said, that was Papa's soft spot. Hey there, Mister Henry, how are them boys of yours comin' along?" You know, Buddy and Papa. "You got some boys there that's fine musicians. That Dodie..." He used to call me Dodie, a nickname. "That Dodie gonna be a good clarinet-man, a good stick-man," and he said "That boy on violin..." "Violean" or something he called it. "Here's a new tune we're playing." And he'd pull out his trumpet, pull out his cornet and blow it, and maybe Papa would get his harmonica.
You're darn right he could read.

Yes, sir. He could read. And Papa would listen to him, and say, "Hey, Mister Henry, my rubber heels is kind of wearing here." Papa said, "Pull off your shoes there, Buddy, I'll put you a pad on there."
